propositions: Type-tier comparability (epic tier 2, story tier 1, task/bug tier 0) causes direct sibling dependencies to escalate incorrectly, resulting in ancestor-child blocking edges never being written (bug 1803).

Redundancy guards are evaluated against the original endpoint pair before promotion, not the pair actually written, allowing invalid ancestor-descendant blocking edges to persist (bug 1803 and jira-reb-1582).

The new structural comparability rule resolves blocking endpoints via their nearest common ancestor (NCA), treating parentless tickets as siblings under a virtual-root sentinel, and recomputes redundancy from the resolved pair only for blocking relations.

Direct children of the same parent now link unchanged with was_redirected false; cross-subtree dependencies escalate to their NCA's direct children, widening escalation to catch previously-silent substitutions.
Type-tier functions (_TYPE_TIER, _tier_of, _tier_of_ticket, _promote_to_tier) are deleted as dead code; _get_ancestors is uncapped and cycle-guarded to walk to root.

The redundancy predicate for blocking relations widens from direct parent-child to any ancestor-descendant pair, closing both the original defect and the post-promotion redundancy gap; non-blocking relations retain the original predicate unchanged.
